tiers.name: syntax
tiers.goal: Type the language without thinking about it.

tiers.name: data
tiers.goal: Know what a value actually is in memory.

tiers.name: organization
tiers.goal: Structure code so it survives being changed.

tiers.name: runtime
tiers.goal: Know what the machine does while your code runs.

tiers.name: patterns
tiers.goal: Recognize the shape of a problem, then pick the idiomatic answer.

variants.name: var with explicit type
variants.when: you want the zero value, or the type is not obvious from the right-hand side

variants.name: short declaration
variants.when: inside a function where the value makes the type obvious

variants.name: naked returns
variants.when: short functions where the names document the result

variants.name: explicit returns
variants.when: anything long enough that you lose track of what is named

variants.name: value receivers
variants.when: small immutable types where copying is cheap and safe

variants.name: pointer receivers
variants.when: mutation, large structs, or any type with a mutex

variants.name: mixed receivers
variants.when: almost never — it confuses the method set rules

variants.name: accept interfaces, return structs
variants.when: library code that must stay flexible for callers

variants.name: small single-method interfaces
variants.when: testing seams and composition, the Go default

variants.name: large service interfaces
variants.when: rarely right; usually a Java habit leaking in

variants.name: sentinel errors
variants.when: callers must test for one specific known failure: errors.Is

variants.name: typed errors
variants.when: callers need structured data off the failure: errors.As

variants.name: opaque wrapped errors
variants.when: the caller only logs it; keeps your internals private

variants.name: Result-style generic type
variants.when: forces handling at the type level, fights every stdlib signature

variants.name: panic and recover
variants.when: truly unrecoverable invariants, and package boundaries only

variants.name: generic function
variants.when: the same algorithm over many types, checked at compile time

variants.name: interface parameter
variants.when: behaviour varies per type; dynamic dispatch is the point

variants.name: any plus type switch
variants.when: few known types, and you want them all in one place

variants.name: code generation
variants.when: you need per-type optimisation the compiler will not give you

variants.name: channels
variants.when: transferring ownership of data between goroutines

variants.name: mutex over shared state
variants.when: protecting a struct field; usually simpler than a channel

variants.name: errgroup
variants.when: fan-out where the first failure should cancel the rest

variants.name: worker pool
variants.when: bounded concurrency over an unbounded queue of work

variants.name: struct tags
variants.when: the default; declarative and enough for most payloads

variants.name: custom MarshalJSON
variants.when: the wire format genuinely differs from your struct

variants.name: intermediate DTO type
variants.when: the API contract must not move when the domain type does

variants.name: code generation
variants.when: hot paths where reflection cost actually shows in a profile

variants.name: functional options
variants.when: many optional settings, and the API must stay additive

variants.name: config struct
variants.when: few settings, all known up front; far less machinery

variants.name: builder with method chaining
variants.when: rare in Go; reads well but hides the error path

variants.name: variadic plain args
variants.when: two or three options that will never grow

variants.name: repository interface
variants.when: you need to swap or fake the store in tests

variants.name: direct queries in the service
variants.when: small services where the indirection buys nothing

variants.name: query object
variants.when: complex read paths that do not fit a CRUD-shaped interface

python.title: Values and Types
mechanism: everything is an object with a refcount
names bind, they do not store

python.title: Control Flow
mechanism: no block scope, only function scope

python.title: Functions
mechanism: default args evaluate once at def time

python.title: Lists, Dicts, Sets
mechanism: dicts are compact and insertion ordered

python.title: Strings
mechanism: str is immutable and sometimes interned

variants.name: plain class
variants.when: behaviour and invariants matter more than the data

variants.name: dataclass
variants.when: records with some behaviour; the default for most value types

variants.name: NamedTuple
variants.when: immutable, tuple-compatible, cheap

variants.name: TypedDict
variants.when: the data is already a dict and must stay one, such as JSON

python.title: Modules and Packages
mechanism: the import system and sys.modules cache

variants.name: Protocol
variants.when: structural typing; the implementer need not know about you

variants.name: ABC
variants.when: you want registration and an explicit inheritance relationship

variants.name: duck typing with no annotation
variants.when: internal code where the contract is obvious

variants.name: raise an exception
variants.when: the Python default; failures propagate until someone cares

variants.name: return None
variants.when: one failure mode, and the caller will obviously check

variants.name: Result type
variants.when: you want the type checker to force handling; fights the ecosystem

variants.name: exception groups
variants.when: concurrent work where several things can fail at once

python.title: Memory and GC
mechanism: reference counting is the primary mechanism
the cycle collector handles the rest

python.title: Concurrency and asyncio
mechanism: the GIL and what it does not protect
the event loop and coroutine scheduling

variants.name: asyncio
variants.when: many concurrent I/O waits in one thread

variants.name: threads
variants.when: blocking I/O in libraries that are not async-aware

variants.name: multiprocessing
variants.when: CPU-bound work under the GIL

variants.name: free-threaded build
variants.when: 3.14 onward; real threads for CPU work, ecosystem still catching up

variants.name: function decorator
variants.when: cross-cutting behaviour with no state

variants.name: class decorator
variants.when: you need to modify the type itself

variants.name: context manager
variants.when: the concern is setup and teardown around a block

variants.name: explicit wrapper call
variants.when: the indirection would hide something the reader needs

scala.title: Values and Types
mechanism: everything is an object, including Int
val is a stable reference, not deep immutability
Any, AnyVal, AnyRef and the unified hierarchy

variants.name: val
variants.when: the default — a binding that will not be reassigned

variants.name: var
variants.when: genuinely mutating local state, and almost nowhere else

variants.name: lazy val
variants.when: expensive to compute and possibly never needed

variants.name: def
variants.when: recomputed on every access; no memoisation

scala.title: Operators and Expressions
mechanism: right-associative methods end in a colon

scala.title: Control Flow
mechanism: if and match are expressions that return values

scala.title: Functions
mechanism: eta-expansion turns a method into a function

scala.title: Collections
mechanism: List is a linked list, Vector is a trie
views are lazy, iterators are single-use

variants.name: List
variants.when: sequential access, pattern matching, prepend-heavy work

variants.name: Vector
variants.when: random access and append; the general-purpose default

variants.name: Array
variants.when: interop with Java, or primitives without boxing

variants.name: LazyList
variants.when: infinite or expensive sequences consumed partially

scala.title: Strings
mechanism: s, f and raw interpolators are compile-time

scala.title: Classes and Objects
mechanism: case classes generate equals, hashCode, copy and unapply
companion objects hold what would be statics
enums in 3 replace sealed trait hierarchies

variants.name: case class
variants.when: immutable data with structural equality; the default

variants.name: plain class
variants.when: identity matters, or you control equality yourself

variants.name: enum
variants.when: a closed set of alternatives — 3's replacement for sealed traits

variants.name: opaque type
variants.when: a zero-cost wrapper that stops a String being any String

scala.title: References and Mutation
mechanism: val prevents reassignment, not mutation of the referent

scala.title: Modules and Packages
mechanism: given instances are found by scope, not import alone

scala.title: Traits and Given
mechanism: type classes are given instances plus extension methods

variants.name: trait
variants.when: shared behaviour an implementer opts into by extending

variants.name: given instance
variants.when: type class evidence supplied at the call site

variants.name: abstract class
variants.when: you need constructor parameters and single inheritance is fine

variants.name: plain function parameter
variants.when: when the indirection buys nothing over passing it

scala.title: Errors
mechanism: exceptions are unchecked on the JVM
Either and Try are values, not control flow

variants.name: Either
variants.when: expected failures with a typed error the caller must handle

variants.name: Try
variants.when: wrapping code that throws, especially Java interop

variants.name: Option
variants.when: absence with no explanation needed

variants.name: throw
variants.when: truly exceptional; the caller is not expected to recover

variants.name: effect type such as IO
variants.when: errors, resources and concurrency handled as one thing

scala.title: Generics
mechanism: context bounds desugar to using parameters
match types compute types from types

scala.title: Concurrency
mechanism: Future needs an ExecutionContext in scope
Future is eager, IO is not
virtual threads change the blocking calculus

variants.name: Future
variants.when: simple async on the stdlib with no dependency

variants.name: cats-effect IO
variants.when: referentially transparent effects, cancellation, resource safety

variants.name: ZIO
variants.when: typed errors and dependencies baked into the effect

variants.name: virtual threads
variants.when: JDK 21 onward; blocking code that no longer costs a thread

scala.title: Serialization
mechanism: no JSON in the standard library

variants.name: circe
variants.when: the common choice; derivation plus a rich combinator API

variants.name: upickle
variants.when: less ceremony and fewer dependencies

variants.name: jsoniter-scala
variants.when: hot paths where allocation actually shows in a profile

variants.name: hand-written codecs
variants.when: the wire format and the domain type genuinely diverge

variants.name: case class with defaults
variants.when: the usual answer; named arguments do the work

variants.name: builder
variants.when: a long construction sequence with validation at the end

variants.name: phantom-typed builder
variants.when: the compiler should reject an incomplete build

variants.name: class
variants.when: identity, inheritance, or instanceof checks actually matter

variants.name: factory function with closures
variants.when: true privacy and no this binding to get wrong

variants.name: plain object plus functions
variants.when: data and behaviour are genuinely separate

variants.name: interface
variants.when: object contracts meant to be extended or augmented

variants.name: type alias
variants.when: unions, intersections, mapped and conditional types

variants.name: branded type
variants.when: you need nominal typing so UserId cannot be an OrderId

variants.name: throw
variants.when: exceptional paths the caller is not expected to handle locally

variants.name: Result union type
variants.when: expected failures you want the compiler to force you to handle

variants.name: discriminated union on a status field
variants.when: several outcomes, not just ok and error

variants.name: null or undefined return
variants.when: one failure mode with no useful detail

variants.name: generic function
variants.when: one implementation across many types

variants.name: function overloads
variants.when: the return type depends on the argument in a non-generic way

variants.name: conditional types
variants.when: the type must be computed from another type

variants.name: async and await
variants.when: the default; sequential-looking code with real error boundaries

variants.name: promise combinators
variants.when: concurrent work: all, allSettled, race, any

variants.name: async iterators
variants.when: streams and paginated sources

variants.name: callbacks
variants.when: legacy interop only

variants.name: JSON.parse plus a type assertion
variants.when: fast and unsafe; you are trusting the source

variants.name: runtime schema validation
variants.when: any external boundary; the assertion is a lie without it

variants.name: hand-written type guards
variants.when: few shapes, no dependency wanted
